tldr: Across all 16 regional headline sets, the story is dual-tracked: Israel struck Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase and conducted follow-on strikes (SECURITY_DEFENSE dominant in most outlets), while Turkey counter-escalated with a genocide charge and Interpol arrest warrant for Netanyahu (CRIME_PUNISHMENT salient in wire services and Mexican coverage). Only Israeli outlets' titles expose a third angle invisible elsewhere: the strikes as Netanyahu's calculated election-era crisis manufacturing.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to frame the Syria strikes as Netanyahu engineering 'constant security crises' for electoral purposes — an explicit political-motive attribution absent from every other outlet's title, which present the strikes as security or diplomatic events.

Only headline to describe 'ground raids' alongside airstrikes, implying a broad multi-domain Israeli military campaign across Syria — a significant scope escalation relative to all other outlets, which confine their headlines to the single Abu al-Duhur airbase strike.

Only headline to foreground Turkey as a 'NATO power' being 'put on notice' — the sole title to flag Turkey's alliance membership as a dimension of the confrontation, an angle no other outlet's headline surfaces.

Only headline to frame the strike as deliberate red-line expansion ('Expanding Its Red Lines in Syria') rather than a reactive security measure, presenting Israeli strikes as a strategic pattern rather than an isolated event.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the story is framed as a simultaneous military escalation and legal confrontation — Israel striking Syria and Turkey responding with an Interpol arrest warrant — while only Haaretz titles expose the domestic political calculation that body-text coverage across other outlets discusses at length.
